transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-04
Start time (UTC): 15:00
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Luis Moreno (Redwood CSM), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Ben Ho (Redwood Support); Rosa Kim (Grovefield VP Eng), Derek Lowe (Head of Data), Aisha Rahman (DevOps), Tom Berger (Security), Samir Patel (SRE)

Summary:
- Runbook walkthrough and ops immersion: network/VPC, secrets/KMS, SSO, and staging perf plan
- Identify immediate blockers for onramp: firewall rules, service account access, sample traffic
- Confirm next steps and owners for pilot staging run

Topics covered: VPC peering and private endpoints, SAML SSO mapping, KMS/HSM key policies, SOC2/attestation expectations (high level), staging benchmark plan, monitoring and alerting hooks, rollback/runbook for failover, cost/latency tradeoffs (batching, quantization)

Action items (covered in call): see metadata above

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Patel: hey everyone, thanks for joining. we wanted to make this pretty practical — runbook, access steps, perf plan — um if anybody needs, like, a quick agenda?
[00:12] Rosa Kim: sounds good, quick agenda please. we've got product and infra on the call so trying to get the exact list of things we'll need to unblock prod staging.
[00:20] Luis Moreno: yep we'll go through runbook sections, network, sso, secrets, then priya will sketch the staging benchmark.
[00:27] Priya Shah: hi all, i'll try to keep to perf and infra notes, and i can post terraform snippets after.
[00:33] Tom Berger: quick ask from security side — what's the list for compliance docs we should expect, and any encryption at rest key management specifics?
[00:42] Maya Patel: great q. high level we have SOC2 Type II certs internal but we'll share the redwood compliance pack, and for keys we support KMS integrations plus customer-managed keys via HSM or cloud KMS — we'll attach the KMS integration guide.
[00:58] Samir Patel: when you say KMS integration, is it a full bring-your-own-key flow or just envelope? want to confirm rotation and separation of duties.
[01:10] Priya Shah: it's BYOK for the private deployment option; for hosted we can do envelope but we also support dedicated where you can hand key policies to your KMS. rotation we support via standard key versioning; we'll add a section in the runbook that maps the exact API calls — sorry, sometimes the auto-transcribe calls it K V cache but that's kay vee cache, not the KMS...
[01:30] Derek Lowe: (laughs) yeah i've seen that. on the perf side: our initial expectation is 200 requests per second peak, payloads average ~4k tokens per request during workflows. is that manageable?
[01:44] Priya Shah: ok 200 rps at 4k tokens is non-trivial; depends on model choice and batch sizing. for contraining latency vs cost we'd recommend a mid-size model with 8-bit quantization and a dedicated pool for the pilot. we can run a staging benchmark to refine.
[02:03] Aisha Rahman: are there auto-scaling considerations? like burst handling is we get higher qps during nightly jobs.
[02:12] Luis Moreno: yes autoscale policies are configurable, and we can set burst capacity windows. for POCs we often start with a dedicated pool and a small burst allowance, then tune based on the benchmark.
[02:25] Tom Berger: what about network — do you require VPC peering or private endpoints? our security team prefers no peering if possible.
[02:34] Maya Patel: we support both. for Private deployment we can be entirely inside your VPC or on-prem; for Dedicated we provide private endpoints and optional VPC peering. we'll include both patterns in the runbook and note firewall ports.
[02:49] Rosa Kim: can you call out what ports/protocols? our infra needs that to get firewall rules approved.
[02:57] Priya Shah: absolutely — typically outbound HTTPS to timber endpoints and a set of internal gRPC ports for the runtime; i'll add the exact port list to the doc. note some customers see the transcribed "g P R C" spelled out oddly in the export, so we'll be explicit.
[03:12] Maya Patel: also note for private cluster installs there are specific NAT and outbound rules for pulling images and kernel modules.
[03:20] Derek Lowe: about samples — we should share a small sample dataset and a traffic trace. who owns that?
[03:27] Maya Patel: grovefield to own sample dataset; Derek if you can send token and qps estimates that's perfect. we'll use those in the staging benchmark.
[03:35] Derek Lowe: yep i'll do that, aiming for EOD tuesday.
[03:40] Priya Shah: for the benchmark plan — here's the quick sketch: small staging cluster with 2 dedicated GPUs, runner with same model variant as desired in prod, run synthetic traffic at 50%, 75%, 100% of expected peak; capture p95 and p99 latencies, CPU/GPU utilization, memory and KV cache hit rates. we'll share a spreadsheet with the fields.
[04:03] Samir Patel: KV cache? are you referring to prefix cache or something else? we need to understand cache invalidation too.
[04:11] Priya Shah: yes prefix/KV cache — sorry the transcript sometimes renders KV as "kay vee" — we'll include caching semantics, TTL, and invalidation notes in the runbook.
[04:24] Aisha Rahman: monitoring — what integrations are available? datadog, prometheus, our existing pager flow.
[04:31] Ben Ho: we emit prometheus metrics out of the runtime and have Datadog overlays; we can drop a sample dashboard and alert rule templates.
[04:39] Tom Berger: SSO — we use SAML 2.0 and Okta; we'll need attribute mapping for RBAC.
[04:46] Luis Moreno: we support SAML and OIDC; we'll provide the SSO mapping checklist and an example metadata XML. also note roles in the console map to RBAC groups — we'll show mapping examples.
[04:58] Rosa Kim: regarding data residency, our compliance folks want logs kept for 90 days and audit trail for admin actions. what's default retention?
[05:07] Maya Patel: default logs retention in hosted is 30 days; for enterprise customers we have extended retention add-ons — we can map a retention plan and exportable audit logs to Grovefield's SIEM. we'll add that section.
[05:20] Samir Patel: any requirements for packet capture during the benchmark? we'd like to capture a few flows to debug latency spikes.
[05:27] Priya Shah: that's fine; we recommend capturing at the ingress, and we can provide an annotation process for matching traces to request IDs.
[05:35] Derek Lowe: ok sounds good. one more on cost: can you provide an expected ballpark for the pilot (the 2 GPU staging)? even a range helps our finance folks.
[05:45] Maya Patel: yes we'll include a pilot cost estimate in the runbook — ballpark depends on model family, quantization, and whether it's hosted or dedicated. we'll include a delta for dedicated vs hosted per 1k tokens.
[05:58] Aisha Rahman: the team is curious about fallback policies — if the dedicated pool is saturated, can requests route to hosted fallback without losing data?
[06:08] Priya Shah: yes we support smart routing with fallback to compatible model variants, but note you'd need to agree on data residency implications. the runbook will show an example policy.
[06:18] Rosa Kim: what's the typical time to stand up a private deployment vs dedicated? we have a month window ideally.
[06:25] Luis Moreno: Dedicated pools often can be provisioned within 2-3 weeks depending on capacity; private on-prem can be 4-8 weeks depending on networking approvals. for the pilot i'd recommend dedicated so you can hit the 1 month mark.
[06:40] Tom Berger: ok that helps. I'll follow up with our procurement and infra to see which path we want.
[06:46] Maya Patel: perfect. next, quick walkthrough of the runbook sections — i'll share my screen (note: recording had some low audio for a sec)
[06:55] [screen share walkthrough, doc references omitted in transcript] 
[08:12] Priya Shah: runbook section 1: access and accounts. steps: create service account, add IP allowlist entries, provide SAML metadata. map of role permissions is included.
[08:30] Aisha Rahman: for service accounts, is there a permission boundary? we want least privilege.
[08:36] Ben Ho: yes we'll provide an IAM policy template with least privilege; some customers further tighten with session policies.
[08:44] Derek Lowe: section 2: networking. the doc shows required outbound endpoints and sample firewall rules.
[08:53] Priya Shah: and a note: if you prefer no peering, we can offer egress-only endpoints with strict IP allowlists.
[09:02] Rosa Kim: section 3: secrets and KMS mapping. please make sure rotation cadence is documented.
[09:10] Maya Patel: will do.
[09:13] [10 minute skip in detailed screen walkthrough - paraphrased in notes] 
[19:20] Priya Shah: perf checklist: we need a small synthetic harness, the model artifact (or name), prompt templates, and expected failure modes; we'll run 3 passes and capture warmup behavior.
[19:35] Derek Lowe: model artifact — we plan to use an open LLM 13B variant, quantized where possible. can the runtime accept custom model artifacts?
[19:44] Priya Shah: yes custom artifacts are supported for Dedicated/Private; hosted catalog has curated variants for faster onboarding. there are a few model packaging caveats we'll note.
[19:55] Samir Patel: how do you handle kernel selection for quantized models? we've seen mismatches lead to perf regressions.
[20:03] Priya Shah: runtime picks kernels based on model arch and seq len; we'll include the compilation matrix. if you have particular model forks, we can run a warm compile in staging.
[20:16] Tom Berger: can we get a short SLA or SLO doc for pilot? uptime and latency targets?
[20:23] Luis Moreno: for pilot we provide availability guidance; formal SLA is part of Dedicated contracts. we'll attach a sample SLO template to the runbook.
[20:33] Rosa Kim: ok, last part - what does success look like for this pilot from Redwood's POV?
[20:40] Maya Patel: success = reproducible p95 latency meeting your target under peak tx, validated autoscale behavior, and seamless handoff to your monitoring and SSO; then we agree on the production roll plan.
[20:53] Derek Lowe: sounds fair.
[20:57] Maya Patel: any other blockers?
[21:01] Tom Berger: procurement questions around contractual language; i'll loop in legal and we may ask for a data processing addendum.
[21:08] Luis Moreno: we have a standard DPA and can start that thread, i'll send the template after.
[21:13] Rosa Kim: one more question — who should be our main point of contact during the staging window?
[21:19] Maya Patel: primary PoC will be Luis for onboarding logistics and Priya for any SE work; Ben will be support contact during the benchmark run.
[21:29] Derek Lowe: ok we'll coordinate dates internally and send the sample artifacts.
[21:33] Maya Patel: great. quick recap: Redwood - share runbook and VPC checklist (Maya), SE to run staging bench (Priya), Grovefield to send traffic profile and datasets (Derek), security to send SSO metadata (Tom). target dates in the notes.
[21:51] Rosa Kim: thanks all, this was helpful. we'll aim to have first artifacts by next Wednesday.
[21:58] Maya Patel: thanks team. we'll follow up in email with the doc and calendar invites for the bench window.

End of transcript.
